‘Inflated’ Hublot Classic Fusion Balloon Dog By Jeff Koons Watches Hands-On

September 16, 2026
12
by Ariel Adams
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:48
Instaread

As someone who has no interest in balloon dogs (artistic or otherwise), I have a lot of positive things to say about what Hublot has done to its Classic Fusion collection in collaboration with Jeff Koons (an American celebrity artist with whom the Swiss watch brand recently formed a relationship). At launch, Hublot has announced two Jeff Koons projects. First are these blue, red, or silver Classic Fusion Balloon Dog by Jeff Koons watches, and second is the much more high-end and elaborate Hublot MP-14 Origin By Jeff Koons. While these instant watches have a retail price of about $25,000 USD, the MP-14 Origin is closer to $500,000 USD. Everything is a limited edition. Let’s take a look at how Hublot “balloonified” its Classic Fusion watches prior to a full collection overhaul that is probably due for 2027.

Whether or not you like Jeff Koons’ Balloon Dog Pop Art, it is an undeniably popular aesthetic that has been produced in numerous colors and sizes, and with installations all over the world. Koons is also one of those rare contemporary artists who has understood the nuances of commercial success and volume manufacturing. He took something popular and expanded upon it, allowing his name and success to permeate the zeitgeist in a way that most living artists probably envy.

Advertising Message

Hublot did not just slap some Balloon Dog elements onto its standard Classic Fusion models, but fundamentally changed much of the Classic Fusion’s case, strap, dial, and even automatic rotor to adapt to the “inflated” aesthetic. The three available limited-edition colors represent some of the most popular Jeff Koons Balloon Dog styles and offer a nice palette for consumers to explore. The red and blue versions of the watch are crafted from anodized aluminum, as that was the only real way to replicate the shiny, colored mirrored texture of the art that inspired the timepieces. The silver version is polished steel. The latter is probably going to be a bit more durable than the aluminum models, but all are priced at the same level.

The Classic Fusion Balloon Dog by Jeff Koons watches are 42mm wide, 11mm thick, and water resistant to 50 meters with a sapphire crystal over the dial. Inside the watches is the Hublot caliber HUB1710 automatic, which is a rebranded Zenith Elite movement. Displaying the time and date, it operates at 4Hz with 50 hours of power reserve. Speaking of the movement, I want to point out something very exciting about it (at least in my opinion). Hublot creates a new “rounded” surface for the special automatic rotor that goes on the movements. This style is meant to go with the inflated balloon theme the rest of the watch enjoys. That said, I think this automatic rotor style is aesthetically superior to the other rotors Hublot often uses, and I would recommend that it carry forward this rotor and use it again for future models. It is just that nice!

Hublot modified so much about the Classic Fusion, including the case, dial, strap, and even the folding buckle deployant to manifest the balloon style. The dial especially looks really fun, and I personally think this is a highly attractive aesthetic. It won’t be to everyone’s tastes, but I think Hublot did a nice job. For what it’s worth, my kids think these watches are super cool-looking. My strong personal recommendation to Hublot is to leave the Balloon Dog elements to this limited-edition series, and moving forward, the brand should create non-limited Classic Fusion Jeff Koons models with merely the inflated elements and nothing related to the balloon dogs.

Advertising Message

Probably the most important and subtle of the Balloon Dog elements is the shape of the inspiration as the counterweight on the central seconds hand. There is also a “Koons” signature on the dial, which actually looks nice. The case is meant to evoke the Balloon Dog as well, but in a manner that I am not super-keen on, personally. That includes the rubber “tail,” which is sticking out at about the 10 o’clock position on the case, as well as the spaced rubber ring around the crown. This latter element looks a lot like a clown nose and is actually quite fragile. I think it would pull off if subjected to the right force. Hublot’s idea was to evoke the Balloon Dog, and it is possible that fans of the recognizable Koons artwork would be into that. Personally, I’m not, and I think the “tail” and the “nose” crown are the weakest elements of the design. Everything else is pretty solid.

The straps that come with these Classic Fusion Balloon Dog by Jeff Koons watches are also very inspired. Hublot says they begin with a rubber base and have a shiny colored polymer insert that is quilted and given the inflated effect. The steel deployant buckle continues the inflated design aesthetic and is one of the neatest features of the overall design. Very nicely done Hublot! As I said earlier, at the outset of the Hublot and Jeff Koons relationship, two models were featured. These limited-edition Classic Fusion Balloon Dog watches are the more obvious commercial watches (given the familiarity with Koons ‘ popular work), and the MP-14 Origin shows a different side of Koons and is a much more original and ambitious creation. aBlogtoWatch will have a different article on the MP-14 with its sapphire case and bracelet, which I recommend you also check out. The three limited-edition Hublot Classic Fusion Balloon Dog by Jeff Koons watches are each limited to 200 pieces. They include the blue anodized aluminum reference 542.UB.5170.NR.JKN26, the red anodized aluminum reference 542.UR.8170.NR.JKN26, and the polished steel reference 542.SX.0820.NR.JKN26. Each has a retail price of $25,100 USD. Learn more at the Hublot website.
